# 1. Data Loading

DDSAnalytics analyzes employee turnover for Frito Lay using 870 labeled employee records. The analysis identifies differences in attrition rates, evaluates KNN and Naive Bayes models, and estimates the cost of prediction errors. The independent competition set contains 300 employees without attrition labels.

```{r data-loading}
required_packages <- c("ggplot2", "caret", "class", "e1071")
missing_packages <- setdiff(required_packages, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing_packages)) stop("Install required packages: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse=", "))
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)
library(class)
library(e1071)

labeled_file <- "CaseStudy1-data.csv"
competition_file <- "CaseStudy1CompSet No Attrition.csv"
stopifnot(file.exists(labeled_file), file.exists(competition_file))
data_eda <- read.csv(labeled_file, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
competition_eda <- read.csv(competition_file, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(data_eda)==870, nrow(competition_eda)==300,
          all(c("ID","Attrition","MonthlyIncome") %in% names(data_eda)),
          !anyDuplicated(data_eda$ID), !anyDuplicated(competition_eda$ID))
cat("Labeled data:", nrow(data_eda), "employees,", ncol(data_eda), "variables\n")
cat("Competition data:", nrow(competition_eda), "employees\n")
cat("Missing values:", sum(is.na(data_eda)), "\n")
cat("Duplicate IDs:", sum(duplicated(data_eda$ID)), "\n")
attrition_counts <- table(data_eda$Attrition)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Attrition=names(attrition_counts),
                        Employees=as.integer(attrition_counts),
                        Percent=round(100*as.numeric(attrition_counts)/nrow(data_eda),2)))
```

# 2. Exploratory Data Analysis

All categorical percentages represent the percentage of employees who left within each category. Numerical plots compare employees who left and stayed.

```{r eda-functions}
cat_vars <- c("BusinessTravel","Department","Education","EducationField",
              "EnvironmentSatisfaction","Gender","JobInvolvement","JobLevel",
              "JobRole","JobSatisfaction","MaritalStatus","OverTime",
              "PerformanceRating","RelationshipSatisfaction","StockOptionLevel",
              "WorkLifeBalance")
num_vars <- c("Age","DailyRate","DistanceFromHome","HourlyRate",
              "MonthlyIncome","MonthlyRate","NumCompaniesWorked","PercentSalaryHike",
              "TotalWorkingYears","TrainingTimesLastYear","YearsAtCompany",
              "YearsInCurrentRole","YearsSinceLastPromotion","YearsWithCurrManager")
stopifnot(all(c(cat_vars,num_vars) %in% names(data_eda)))

rate_by <- function(variable) {
  t <- table(Group=as.character(data_eda[[variable]]), Attrition=data_eda$Attrition)
  n <- rowSums(t)
  yes <- if ("Yes" %in% colnames(t)) t[,"Yes"] else rep(0,length(n))
  data.frame(Group=names(n), Employees=as.integer(n), Leavers=as.integer(yes),
             AttritionRate=100*as.numeric(yes)/as.numeric(n))
}
plot_rate <- function(variable) {
  x <- rate_by(variable)
  ggplot(x,aes(x=reorder(Group,AttritionRate),y=AttritionRate)) +
    geom_col(fill="#53749A") + coord_flip() +
    geom_text(aes(label=sprintf("%.1f%%",AttritionRate)),hjust=-.12,size=3) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,max(x$AttritionRate)*1.25+1)) +
    labs(title=paste("Attrition Rate by",variable),x=NULL,y="Attrition Rate (%)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size=11)
}
plot_box <- function(variable) {
  ggplot(data_eda,aes(x=factor(Attrition,levels=c("No","Yes")),
                      y=.data[[variable]],fill=Attrition)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha=.3) +
    stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point",shape=18,size=2.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=c("No"="#53749A","Yes"="#B34A4A")) +
    guides(fill="none") + labs(title=paste(variable,"by Attrition"),
    subtitle="Diamond indicates group mean",x="Attrition",y=variable) +
    theme_minimal(base_size=11)
}
```

## 2.4 Three Key Attrition Factors

Overtime, job involvement, and job role were selected from the observed rate differences and their relevance to employee retention. They are associations, not causal effects.

# 3. KNN Classification

Four predictors: Age, YearsInCurrentRole, OverTime, and JobRole. The model uses k = 29 and an attrition-vote threshold of 0.20. The split is stratified at 80/20 (training/holdout); repeated training-set validation uses 500 splits.

```{r knn-final-code, echo=TRUE, results="hide", fig.show="hide"}
SEED <- 6306
K <- 29
THRESHOLD <- 0.20
FEATURES <- c("Age", "YearsInCurrentRole", "OverTime", "JobRole")

set.seed(SEED)

train_path <- "CaseStudy1-data.csv"
competition_path <- "CaseStudy1CompSet No Attrition.csv"

stopifnot(file.exists(train_path))
stopifnot(file.exists(competition_path))

df <- read.csv(train_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
competition <- read.csv(competition_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

stopifnot(
  all(c("ID", "Attrition", FEATURES) %in% names(df)),
  all(c("ID", FEATURES) %in% names(competition)),
  nrow(competition) == 300L,
  !anyDuplicated(df$ID),
  !anyDuplicated(competition$ID)
)

df$Attrition <- factor(df$Attrition, levels = c("Yes", "No"))

for (v in c("OverTime", "JobRole")) {
  levels_v <- sort(unique(c(
    as.character(df[[v]]),
    as.character(competition[[v]])
  )))
  
  df[[v]] <- factor(df[[v]], levels = levels_v)
  competition[[v]] <- factor(competition[[v]], levels = levels_v)
}

for (v in c("Age", "YearsInCurrentRole")) {
  df[[v]] <- as.numeric(df[[v]])
  competition[[v]] <- as.numeric(competition[[v]])
}

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(df[, c("ID", "Attrition", FEATURES)]),
  !anyNA(competition[, c("ID", FEATURES)])
)

cat("\n========== ATTRITION DISTRIBUTION ==========\n")
print(table(df$Attrition))
print(round(100 * prop.table(table(df$Attrition)), 2))

set.seed(SEED)

train_index <- createDataPartition(
  df$Attrition,
  p = 0.80,
  list = FALSE
)

train <- df[train_index, , drop = FALSE]
test <- df[-train_index, , drop = FALSE]

cat("\n========== DATA SPLIT ==========\n")
cat("Training:", nrow(train), "\n")
cat("Holdout:", nrow(test), "\n")

prepare_knn <- function(training, testing) {
  
  dummies <- dummyVars(
    ~ .,
    data = training[, FEATURES, drop = FALSE],
    fullRank = FALSE
  )
  
  x_train <- as.matrix(predict(
    dummies,
    newdata = training[, FEATURES, drop = FALSE]
  ))
  
  x_test <- as.matrix(predict(
    dummies,
    newdata = testing[, FEATURES, drop = FALSE]
  ))
  
  stopifnot(
    identical(colnames(x_train), colnames(x_test)),
    all(is.finite(x_train)),
    all(is.finite(x_test))
  )
  
  mu <- colMeans(x_train)
  sigma <- apply(x_train, 2, sd)
  sigma[!is.finite(sigma) | sigma < 1e-8] <- 1
  
  x_train <- sweep(
    sweep(x_train, 2, mu, "-"),
    2, sigma, "/"
  )
  
  x_test <- sweep(
    sweep(x_test, 2, mu, "-"),
    2, sigma, "/"
  )
  
  list(train = x_train, test = x_test)
}

predict_knn <- function(training, testing, seed = SEED) {
  
  stopifnot(
    nrow(training) >= K,
    nrow(testing) >= 1L
  )
  
  x <- prepare_knn(training, testing)
  
  set.seed(seed)
  
  pred <- class::knn(
    train = x$train,
    test = x$test,
    cl = training$Attrition,
    k = K,
    prob = TRUE
  )
  
  vote <- as.numeric(attr(pred, "prob"))
  
  p_yes <- ifelse(
    as.character(pred) == "Yes",
    vote,
    1 - vote
  )
  
  stopifnot(
    length(p_yes) == nrow(testing),
    all(is.finite(p_yes))
  )
  
  as.numeric(p_yes)
}

evaluate_knn <- function(actual, probability) {
  
  actual <- factor(actual, levels = c("Yes", "No"))
  
  predicted <- factor(
    ifelse(probability >= THRESHOLD, "Yes", "No"),
    levels = c("Yes", "No")
  )
  
  cm <- confusionMatrix(
    predicted,
    actual,
    positive = "Yes"
  )
  
  sensitivity <- unname(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"])
  specificity <- unname(cm$byClass["Specificity"])
  precision <- unname(cm$byClass["Pos Pred Value"])
  
  f1 <- if (
    is.na(precision) ||
    is.na(sensitivity) ||
    precision + sensitivity == 0
  ) {
    0
  } else {
    2 * precision * sensitivity / (precision + sensitivity)
  }
  
  metrics <- data.frame(
    Accuracy = unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    Sensitivity = sensitivity,
    Specificity = specificity,
    Precision = precision,
    F1 = f1,
    BalancedAccuracy = (sensitivity + specificity) / 2,
    CombinedScore = sensitivity + specificity
  )
  
  list(
    metrics = metrics,
    confusion_matrix = cm,
    predictions = predicted
  )
}

set.seed(SEED)

iterations <- 500
splitPerc <- 0.80

validation_results <- data.frame(
  Accuracy = numeric(iterations),
  Sensitivity = numeric(iterations),
  Specificity = numeric(iterations),
  Precision = numeric(iterations),
  F1 = numeric(iterations),
  BalancedAccuracy = numeric(iterations),
  CombinedScore = numeric(iterations)
)

for (i in seq_len(iterations)) {
  
  train_indices <- sample(
    seq_len(nrow(train)),
    size = round(splitPerc * nrow(train))
  )
  
  tr <- train[train_indices, , drop = FALSE]
  va <- train[-train_indices, , drop = FALSE]
  
  p <- predict_knn(
    training = tr,
    testing = va,
    seed = SEED + i
  )
  
  result <- evaluate_knn(
    actual = va$Attrition,
    probability = p
  )
  
  validation_results[i, ] <- result$metrics[1, ]
}

cv_metrics <- as.data.frame(
  lapply(validation_results, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
)

cv_result <- list(
  metrics = cv_metrics,
  validation_results = validation_results
)

cat("\n========== REPEATED VALIDATION ==========\n")
cat("Method: Repeated Random 80/20 Train/Test Split\n")
cat("Iterations:", iterations, "\n")
cat("K:", K, "| Threshold:", THRESHOLD, "\n")

print(
  cv_result$metrics,
  row.names = FALSE,
  digits = 4
)

plot(
  seq_len(iterations),
  validation_results$Accuracy,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "Iteration",
  ylab = "Accuracy",
  main = "KNN: Repeated Validation Accuracy"
)

abline(
  h = mean(validation_results$Accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
  col = "red",
  lty = 2
)

train_probability <- predict_knn(train, train)
train_result <- evaluate_knn(
  actual = train$Attrition,
  probability = train_probability
)

cat("\n========== TRAINING SET PERFORMANCE (IN-SAMPLE) ==========\n")
print(train_result$metrics, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
cat("\n========== TRAINING SET CONFUSION MATRIX ==========\n")
print(train_result$confusion_matrix)

holdout_probability <- predict_knn(train, test)

holdout_result <- evaluate_knn(
  test$Attrition,
  holdout_probability
)

performance <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    Dataset = "Training (in-sample)",
    train_result$metrics
  ),
  data.frame(
    Dataset = "Repeated Random Split",
    cv_result$metrics
  ),
  data.frame(
    Dataset = "Holdout Test",
    holdout_result$metrics
  )
)

cat("\n========== KNN MODEL ==========\n")
cat("Features:", paste(FEATURES, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("K:", K, "| Threshold:", THRESHOLD, "\n")

cat("\n========== PERFORMANCE ==========\n")
print(
  performance,
  row.names = FALSE,
  digits = 4
)

cat("\n========== HOLDOUT CONFUSION MATRIX ==========\n")
print(holdout_result$confusion_matrix)

cat("\n========== VALIDATION REQUIREMENT ==========\n")

print(data.frame(
  Dataset = performance$Dataset,
  Sensitivity_Pass = performance$Sensitivity > 0.60,
  Specificity_Pass = performance$Specificity > 0.60
), row.names = FALSE)

competition_probability <- predict_knn(df, competition)

submission <- data.frame(
  ID = competition$ID,
  Attrition = ifelse(
    competition_probability >= THRESHOLD,
    "Yes",
    "No"
  )
)

submission <- submission[
  order(submission$ID),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(submission) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(submission) == 300L,
  identical(names(submission), c("ID", "Attrition")),
  !anyNA(submission),
  !anyDuplicated(submission$ID),
  all(submission$Attrition %in% c("Yes", "No"))
)

output_file <- "Case1PredictionsCho_KNN_Comparison.csv"

write.csv(
  submission,
  output_file,
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("\n========== COMPETITION PREDICTIONS ==========\n")
cat("Output:", normalizePath(output_file), "\n")
cat("Prediction Distribution:\n")
print(table(submission$Attrition))
```

```{r save-knn-state, include=FALSE}
knn_train_metrics <- train_result$metrics
knn_cv_metrics <- cv_result$metrics
knn_validation_results <- validation_results
knn_holdout <- holdout_result
knn_test <- test
knn_train <- train
knn_comp_prediction <- submission
```

# 4. Naive Bayes Classification

Eight predictors: Age, DistanceFromHome, YearsAtCompany, JobInvolvement, WorkLifeBalance, BusinessTravel, OverTime, and JobRole. The model uses Laplace = 1 and an attrition-probability threshold of 0.21.

```{r nb-final-code, echo=TRUE, results="hide", fig.show="hide"}
SEED <- 6306
LAPLACE <- 1
THRESHOLD <- 0.21

FEATURES <- c(
  "Age",
  "DistanceFromHome",
  "YearsAtCompany",
  "JobInvolvement",
  "WorkLifeBalance",
  "BusinessTravel",
  "OverTime",
  "JobRole"
)

CATEGORICAL <- c("BusinessTravel", "OverTime", "JobRole")

set.seed(SEED)

train_path <- "CaseStudy1-data.csv"
competition_path <- "CaseStudy1CompSet No Attrition.csv"

stopifnot(file.exists(train_path))
stopifnot(file.exists(competition_path))

df <- read.csv(train_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
competition <- read.csv(competition_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

stopifnot(
  all(c("ID", "Attrition", FEATURES) %in% names(df)),
  all(c("ID", FEATURES) %in% names(competition)),
  nrow(competition) == 300L,
  !anyDuplicated(df$ID),
  !anyDuplicated(competition$ID)
)

df$Attrition <- factor(df$Attrition, levels = c("Yes", "No"))

for (v in CATEGORICAL) {
  levels_v <- sort(unique(c(
    as.character(df[[v]]),
    as.character(competition[[v]])
  )))
  
  df[[v]] <- factor(df[[v]], levels = levels_v)
  competition[[v]] <- factor(competition[[v]], levels = levels_v)
}

for (v in setdiff(FEATURES, CATEGORICAL)) {
  df[[v]] <- as.numeric(df[[v]])
  competition[[v]] <- as.numeric(competition[[v]])
}

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(df[, c("ID", "Attrition", FEATURES)]),
  !anyNA(competition[, c("ID", FEATURES)])
)

cat("\n========== ATTRITION DISTRIBUTION ==========\n")
print(table(df$Attrition))
print(round(100 * prop.table(table(df$Attrition)), 2))

set.seed(SEED)

train_index <- createDataPartition(
  df$Attrition,
  p = 0.80,
  list = FALSE
)

train <- df[train_index, , drop = FALSE]
test <- df[-train_index, , drop = FALSE]

cat("\n========== DATA SPLIT ==========\n")
cat("Training:", nrow(train), "\n")
cat("Holdout:", nrow(test), "\n")

predict_nb <- function(training, testing) {
  
  model <- e1071::naiveBayes(
    x = training[, FEATURES, drop = FALSE],
    y = training$Attrition,
    laplace = LAPLACE
  )
  
  probabilities <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = testing[, FEATURES, drop = FALSE],
    type = "raw"
  )
  
  p_yes <- as.numeric(probabilities[, "Yes"])
  
  stopifnot(
    length(p_yes) == nrow(testing),
    all(is.finite(p_yes))
  )
  
  p_yes
}

evaluate_nb <- function(actual, probability) {
  
  actual <- factor(actual, levels = c("Yes", "No"))
  
  predicted <- factor(
    ifelse(probability >= THRESHOLD, "Yes", "No"),
    levels = c("Yes", "No")
  )
  
  cm <- confusionMatrix(
    predicted,
    actual,
    positive = "Yes"
  )
  
  sensitivity <- unname(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"])
  specificity <- unname(cm$byClass["Specificity"])
  precision <- unname(cm$byClass["Pos Pred Value"])
  
  tp <- sum(predicted == "Yes" & actual == "Yes")
  fp <- sum(predicted == "Yes" & actual == "No")
  fn <- sum(predicted == "No" & actual == "Yes")
  
  f1 <- if ((2 * tp + fp + fn) == 0) {
    0
  } else {
    2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn)
  }
  
  metrics <- data.frame(
    Accuracy = unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    Sensitivity = sensitivity,
    Specificity = specificity,
    Precision = precision,
    F1 = f1,
    BalancedAccuracy = (sensitivity + specificity) / 2,
    CombinedScore = sensitivity + specificity
  )
  
  list(
    metrics = metrics,
    confusion_matrix = cm,
    predictions = predicted
  )
}

set.seed(SEED)

iterations <- 500
splitPerc <- 0.80

validation_results <- data.frame(
  Accuracy = numeric(iterations),
  Sensitivity = numeric(iterations),
  Specificity = numeric(iterations),
  Precision = numeric(iterations),
  F1 = numeric(iterations),
  BalancedAccuracy = numeric(iterations),
  CombinedScore = numeric(iterations)
)

for (i in seq_len(iterations)) {
  
  train_indices <- sample(
    seq_len(nrow(train)),
    size = round(splitPerc * nrow(train))
  )
  
  tr <- train[train_indices, , drop = FALSE]
  va <- train[-train_indices, , drop = FALSE]
  
  p <- predict_nb(
    training = tr,
    testing = va
  )
  
  result <- evaluate_nb(
    actual = va$Attrition,
    probability = p
  )
  
  validation_results[i, ] <- result$metrics[1, ]
}

cv_metrics <- as.data.frame(
  lapply(validation_results, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
)

cv_result <- list(
  metrics = cv_metrics,
  validation_results = validation_results
)

cat("\n========== REPEATED VALIDATION ==========\n")
cat("Method: Repeated Random 80/20 Train/Test Split\n")
cat("Iterations:", iterations, "\n")
cat("Laplace:", LAPLACE, "| Threshold:", THRESHOLD, "\n")

print(
  cv_result$metrics,
  row.names = FALSE,
  digits = 4
)

plot(
  seq_len(iterations),
  validation_results$Accuracy,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "Iteration",
  ylab = "Accuracy",
  main = "Naive Bayes: Repeated Validation Accuracy"
)

abline(
  h = mean(validation_results$Accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
  col = "red",
  lty = 2
)

train_probability <- predict_nb(train, train)
train_result <- evaluate_nb(
  actual = train$Attrition,
  probability = train_probability
)

cat("\n========== TRAINING SET PERFORMANCE (IN-SAMPLE) ==========\n")
print(train_result$metrics, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
cat("\n========== TRAINING SET CONFUSION MATRIX ==========\n")
print(train_result$confusion_matrix)

holdout_probability <- predict_nb(train, test)

holdout_result <- evaluate_nb(
  actual = test$Attrition,
  probability = holdout_probability
)

performance <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    Dataset = "Training (in-sample)",
    train_result$metrics
  ),
  data.frame(
    Dataset = "Repeated Random Split",
    cv_result$metrics
  ),
  data.frame(
    Dataset = "Holdout Test",
    holdout_result$metrics
  )
)

cat("\n========== NAIVE BAYES MODEL ==========\n")
cat("Features:", paste(FEATURES, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Laplace:", LAPLACE, "| Threshold:", THRESHOLD, "\n")

cat("\n========== PERFORMANCE ==========\n")
print(
  performance,
  row.names = FALSE,
  digits = 4
)

cat("\n========== HOLDOUT CONFUSION MATRIX ==========\n")
print(holdout_result$confusion_matrix)

cat("\n========== VALIDATION REQUIREMENT ==========\n")

print(
  data.frame(
    Dataset = performance$Dataset,
    Sensitivity_Pass = performance$Sensitivity > 0.60,
    Specificity_Pass = performance$Specificity > 0.60
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

competition_probability <- predict_nb(df, competition)

submission <- data.frame(
  ID = competition$ID,
  Attrition = ifelse(
    competition_probability >= THRESHOLD,
    "Yes",
    "No"
  )
)

submission <- submission[
  order(submission$ID),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(submission) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(submission) == 300L,
  identical(names(submission), c("ID", "Attrition")),
  !anyNA(submission),
  !anyDuplicated(submission$ID),
  all(submission$Attrition %in% c("Yes", "No"))
)

output_file <- "Case1PredictionsCho Attrition.csv"

write.csv(
  submission,
  output_file,
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("\n========== COMPETITION PREDICTIONS ==========\n")
cat("Output:", normalizePath(output_file), "\n")
cat("Prediction Distribution:\n")
print(table(submission$Attrition))
```

# 5. Model Comparison

Sensitivity measures the share of actual leavers correctly identified. Specificity measures the share of employees who stayed correctly identified. A false positive is an employee incorrectly flagged as leaving; a false negative is a departing employee missed by the model.

```{r performance-summary}
make_row <- function(model, split, metrics) {
  data.frame(Model=model, Evaluation=split,
             Accuracy=100*metrics$Accuracy, Sensitivity=100*metrics$Sensitivity,
             Specificity=100*metrics$Specificity, Precision=100*metrics$Precision,
             F1=100*metrics$F1, SensPlusSpec=100*metrics$CombinedScore,
             Meets60Pct=ifelse(metrics$Sensitivity>.6 & metrics$Specificity>.6,"PASS","FAIL"))
}
performance_table <- rbind(
  make_row("KNN","Training (in-sample)",knn_train_metrics),
  make_row("KNN","Repeated splits (mean)",knn_cv_metrics),
  make_row("KNN","Holdout",knn_holdout$metrics),
  make_row("Naive Bayes","Training (in-sample)",nb_train_metrics),
  make_row("Naive Bayes","Repeated splits (mean)",nb_cv_metrics),
  make_row("Naive Bayes","Holdout",nb_holdout$metrics))
knitr::kable(performance_table,digits=2,
             caption="Performance percentages; criterion requires BOTH sensitivity and specificity >60%")
```

```{r matrices}
cat("KNN holdout confusion matrix\n")
print(knn_holdout$confusion_matrix$table)
cat("\nNaive Bayes holdout confusion matrix\n")
print(nb_holdout$confusion_matrix$table)
```

# 6. Financial Analysis

For the scenario below, every employee predicted to leave is offered $200. The calculation assumes that correctly flagged leavers accept the incentive and remain employed. Missed leavers generate a replacement cost of 50%, 100%, 200%, or 400% of annual income. These figures are hypothetical, not observed savings.

```{r economics}
financial_rows <- function(model_name, predicted, actual, monthly_income, rate) {
  truth <- as.character(actual)
  pred <- as.character(predicted)
  salary <- 12 * monthly_income
  flagged <- sum(pred=="Yes")
  fn <- pred=="No" & truth=="Yes"
  base <- sum(salary[truth=="Yes"])*rate
  cost <- 200*flagged + rate*sum(salary[fn])
  data.frame(Model=model_name, ReplacementRate=paste0(rate*100,"%"),
             TP=sum(pred=="Yes" & truth=="Yes"), FP=sum(pred=="Yes" & truth=="No"),
             FN=sum(fn), Flagged=flagged,
             IncentiveCost=200*flagged, FNSalary=sum(salary[fn]),
             NoInterventionBaseline=base, TotalEstimatedCost=cost,
             PotentialSavings=base-cost)
}
stopifnot(identical(as.character(knn_test$Attrition),as.character(nb_test$Attrition)),
          identical(knn_test$ID, nb_test$ID))
scenarios <- do.call(rbind,lapply(c(.5,1,2,4),function(r) {
  rbind(financial_rows("KNN",knn_holdout$predictions,knn_test$Attrition,knn_test$MonthlyIncome,r),
        financial_rows("Naive Bayes",nb_holdout$predictions,nb_test$Attrition,nb_test$MonthlyIncome,r))
}))
knitr::kable(scenarios[,c("Model","ReplacementRate","TP","FP","FN","Flagged","IncentiveCost","FNSalary","TotalEstimatedCost","PotentialSavings")],
             format.args=list(big.mark=","),caption="Holdout-based financial scenarios (USD assumptions)")
```

```{r cost-comparison}
k <- scenarios[scenarios$Model=="KNN",]
n <- scenarios[scenarios$Model=="Naive Bayes",]
comparison_cost <- data.frame(ReplacementCostAssumption=k$ReplacementRate,
                              KNN_Total_Cost=k$TotalEstimatedCost,
                              NaiveBayes_Total_Cost=n$TotalEstimatedCost,
                              KNN_Cost_Advantage=n$TotalEstimatedCost-k$TotalEstimatedCost)
knitr::kable(comparison_cost,format.args=list(big.mark=","),
             caption="KNN estimated cost advantage relative to Naive Bayes")
```

The holdout model with better classification performance is not necessarily the model with the lowest assumed replacement cost: the annual salary of each missed leaver also affects the result.

# 7. Competition Predictions

The final Naive Bayes model is fit to all 870 labeled employees and generates 300 predictions, sorted by ID. Submit `Case1PredictionsCho Attrition.csv`.

```{r verify-submission}
submission_file <- "Case1PredictionsCho Attrition.csv"
stopifnot(file.exists(submission_file))
final_predictions <- read.csv(submission_file,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(final_predictions)==300L,
          identical(names(final_predictions),c("ID","Attrition")),
          identical(order(final_predictions$ID),seq_len(nrow(final_predictions))),
          all(final_predictions$Attrition %in% c("Yes","No")),
          !anyNA(final_predictions), !anyDuplicated(final_predictions$ID))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(final_predictions$Attrition)),col.names=c("Predicted Attrition","Count"),
             caption="Unlabeled competition-set prediction distribution")
```

# 8. Results and Presentation

The overall attrition rate is 16.1% (140 of 870). Overtime employees show 31.7% attrition compared with 9.7% without overtime. The lowest job involvement category has 46.8% attrition compared with 8.6% in the highest. Sales Representatives have 45.3% attrition.

On the 174-person holdout, both models identify 20 of 28 leavers (71.43% sensitivity). Naive Bayes achieves 82.76% accuracy and 84.93% specificity, compared with KNN's 77.59% accuracy and 78.77% specificity. Naive Bayes is used for the competition prediction file; the retention-cost estimates depend on the stated incentive assumption.
